chunks: And Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said:
The marketplace of the Muslims is like their mosque. So whoever reaches a place first has more right to it until the night.

key_terms.أَحَقُّ: more entitled; having the stronger right of temporary use
key_terms.اللَّيْلِ: night; the limit of that priority
key_terms.الْمُسْلِمِينَ: the Muslims; indicating the shared communal nature of the market
key_terms.سَبَقَ: arrived first; establishing priority by precedence
key_terms.سُوقُ: marketplace; the public place of trade being discussed
key_terms.كَمَسْجِدِهِمْ: like their mosque; a comparison to a common space open to all
key_terms.مَكَانٍ: a place or spot within the marketplace

ai.seo_question: Who has priority over a place in the Muslim marketplace according to Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states a rule of shared public use in the Muslim marketplace, comparing it to the mosque in that no one has a stronger claim over an open spot than the one who arrives first. It indicates an orderly and fair basis for temporary occupancy in communal commercial spaces.
